emergence.summary: A dominantly inherited multisystem hamartoma syndrome caused by loss-of-function of either subunit of an obligate signalling BRAKE. TSC1 (hamartin) and TSC2 (tuberin) form the TSC protein complex, the GTPase-activating-protein (GAP) that keeps the small GTPase Rheb in its inactive GDP state and so RESTRAINS mechanistic-target-of-rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), the master growth/anabolism kinase hub. The functional brake is the TSC1/TSC2 complex, so biallelic (two-hit, germline + somatic) LOF of EITHER subunit disables the same GAP -> Rheb stays GTP-loaded -> mTORC1 is constitutively over-active -> protein/lipid synthesis and cell growth run unrestrained -> hamartomas across brain (cortical tubers, subependymal giant-cell astrocytoma/SEGA, epilepsy), kidney (angiomyolipoma), heart (rhabdomyoma), skin and lung (lymphangioleiomyomatosis). Read as a released BRAKE on mTORC1 (the TSC1/TSC2 complex brakes Rheb-mTORC1; LOF releases it -> signalling UP) -- the released-brake -> over-activation convention (tyrosinaemia / haemochromatosis / sitosterolaemia) carried onto a NEW INTRACELLULAR SIGNALLING (mTOR / growth-regulation) axis, and the kit's FOURTH TWO-CAUSAL-GENE convergence (after HCM, sitosterolaemia, cystinuria) where both subunits perturb the SAME axis UP (the deeper switch, TSC2, is picked as primary). The kit re-derives the targeted approved arm -- RESTRAIN the over-active node with an mTOR inhibitor (everolimus / sirolimus), which inhibits mTORC1 directly and so lowers the over-driven growth output even though the TSC1/TSC2 GAP remains broken (the upstream/parallel-node restraint logic). Everolimus is approved for TSC-associated SEGA, renal angiomyolipoma and refractory seizures; it modifies the pathway, is not curative, and the neurocognitive (TSC-associated neuropsychiatric / autism) burden is incompletely addressed (recorded honestly). The gamma reads the TSC1 and TSC2 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice/deletion two-hit events outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: mTORC1 signalling output (cell growth / anabolism -> hamartomatous tissue overgrowth) -- a growth-regulation / mTOR-pathway axis; the released-brake -> over-activation read on an intracellular signalling pathway, the signalling contrast to the kit's metabolite/level/transport axes

per_gene.note: TSC2 encodes tuberin, the obligate partner subunit that carries the catalytic GAP domain acting on Rheb; the functional brake is the TSC1/TSC2 heterodimer, so two-hit LOF of TSC2 disables Rheb GAP activity just as TSC1 loss does -> the same released-brake -> mTORC1 over-activation (axis UP). TSC2 mutations are generally commoner and more severe than TSC1. 16p13.3 (contiguous with PKD1), OMIM 191092; TSC2 disease OMIM 613254. NCBI official symbol TSC2. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding/splice/large-deletion lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
per_gene.src: European Chromosome 16 TSC Consortium 1993 Cell 75:1305 (TSC2/tuberin identified); Inoki 2003 Nat Cell Biol 5:578 (tuberin is the Rheb GAP)

per_gene.note: TSC1 encodes hamartin, one subunit of the TSC1/TSC2 GTPase-activating-protein complex that holds Rheb inactive (GDP) and so RESTRAINS mTORC1 -- a BRAKE on growth signalling. Hamartin stabilises tuberin and localises the complex; two-hit LOF disables the shared GAP -> Rheb-GTP -> mTORC1 over-activation (axis UP). 9q34.13, OMIM 605284; TSC1 disease OMIM 191100. NCBI official symbol TSC1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice/deletion lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
per_gene.src: van Slegtenhorst 1997 Science 277:805 (TSC1/hamartin identified); Tee 2003 Curr Biol 13:1259 (TSC1/TSC2 is the Rheb GAP braking mTORC1)

levers.push_direction: inhibit mTORC1 (rapalogue) to lower the over-active growth-signalling output -> push the axis DOWN toward healthy and shrink the hamartomas; bypasses the broken TSC1/TSC2 GAP brake by acting at the downstream kinase node
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of mTORC1 suppression / lesion volume reduction / seizure change not derived from sequence
levers.src: Krueger 2010 NEJM 363:1801 (everolimus shrinks SEGA); Bissler 2013 Lancet 381:817 (everolimus, renal angiomyolipoma); French 2016 Lancet 388:2153 (everolimus, TSC seizures); everolimus FDA TSC indications

levers.push_direction: restore the TSC1/TSC2 GAP brake on Rheb-mTORC1 so the pathway is no longer over-driven -> the NET axis effect is to RESTRAIN the over-shoot back toward normal (gene/function restoration of the deeper causal subunit; restrain-coded by net axis effect, the Wilson/cystinosis convention)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree/durability of restored GAP braking not derived from sequence
levers.src: Inoki 2003 Nat Cell Biol 5:578 (tuberin GAP function as the restoration target); investigational, no approved TSC gene therapy

falsifiers.claim: TSC1 or TSC2 LOF (released Rheb GAP brake) raises mTORC1 signalling output (axis UP)
falsifiers.falsifier: a TSC1 or TSC2 LOF allele that LOWERED mTORC1 activity (e.g. reduced phospho-S6K1/S6/4E-BP1) or REDUCED Rheb-GTP loading would refute the released-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: phospho-S6K1 / phospho-S6 / phospho-4E-BP1 immunoassay and Rheb-GTP loading in TSC1- or TSC2-null cells vs wild-type

falsifiers.claim: restraining mTORC1 (mTOR inhibition) is the CORRECTIVE direction (lowers the over-active growth output)
falsifiers.falsifier: if an mTOR inhibitor RAISED mTORC1 output or ENLARGED TSC hamartomas, the restrain-mTORC1 lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: SEGA / renal angiomyolipoma volume and phospho-S6 response to everolimus/sirolimus in TSC
